analysis:
Examined all supplied test source, patches and metadata against the indexed model and detailed T-041. No concrete security regression is supported by these test-only changes. DistributedInstalledCancellationTests.swift:9–26 adds Gemma tensor-parallel independent retirement expectations for 2–8 lanes, including both image flags, while retaining singleton defaults. DistributedInstalledLanesTests.swift:17–23 verifies explicit Gemma lanes; :49–53 replaces blanket tensor-parallel exclusion with adapter-specific defaults. These assertions describe policy, not proof of native cancellation or isolation.
InstalledSessionCheck.swift:978–1345 is unchanged surrounding source per the complete range map. It exercises artifact-specific public grants, capability mismatch refusal, bounded probes, epoch/rank credentials, batched cancellation, cleanup/release fencing, lease renewal and quarantine on missing release. Fixture plaintext endpoints are explicitly test stand-ins, not evidence of production plaintext exposure. The orientation patch moves loopback test listeners to ephemeral ports with retries, reducing collisions; the complete helper and other changed sections are outside these units.
Integration should reconcile Gemma lane eligibility with the changed planner/native implementation: cancellation must retire only the selected request without disrupting collectives or reusing live KV resources (T-010, TB-007, A-018), and image-bearing requests must either be excluded upstream or supported safely. Verify any related cache-scope/key plumbing preserves T-041 and A-001 isolation; the environment/key assertions at InstalledSessionCheck.swift:1021–1028 do not establish that production contract. No supplied change alters attestation, serving authorization, billing, privileged helpers or credential custody. Runtime validation and the remaining changed test sections are coverage limits, not observed missing controls.
